title: AI Voice & TTS News Briefing
summary: Covers Mon Nov 16, 7:52 AM to Tue Nov 17, 7:52 AM MT. Two new developments: ElevenLabs is acquiring Kotoba Technologies, maker of the Koto Japanese TTS, speech recognition and speech-to-speech interpretation models (HIGH IMPACT); and France's CNC no longer funds AI-only dubbing, subtitling or audio description (in force Nov 1; first reported here). Today Google shuts down five preview Gemini voice models.

articles.title: HIGH IMPACT: ElevenLabs to acquire Kotoba, Japan's Koto voice AI lab
articles.summary: ElevenLabs agreed to acquire Kotoba Technologies, whose Koto model handles Japanese text-to-speech, speech-to-text and speech-to-speech for simultaneous interpretation and already powers Japanese conversations in Salesforce Agentforce Voice. Closing is expected later in Q4 2026; terms not disclosed (press reports of about $100M are unconfirmed). Kotoba plans to improve Japanese first, then Korean and other East Asian languages. Why it matters: Japanese and Korean quality (pitch accent, honorifics, mixed scripts, name reading) should improve in a major TTS/dubbing vendor, and the move signals vendors are buying language-specific depth rather than relying on one global model; re-test Japanese output after the deal closes.

articles.title: France's CNC stops funding AI-only dubbing, subtitling and audio description
articles.source: Journal officiel (Légifrance), CNC deliberation 2026/CA/28; reported by Slator Nov 16
articles.summary: Under a new rule in force Nov 1 for new funding applications, France's national film and media agency counts only payments to human script writers, voice actors and subtitle authors, plus related recording, mixing and sync costs, toward subsidized dubbing, voice-over, audio description and subtitling. AI tools are not banned, but AI-only localization gets no public money. French dubbing groups call it a first step and want it extended to foreign films and streamers. Why it matters: the first national public-funding rule tying dubbing and audio-description support to human performers, a template other European funders and unions may push; human-in-the-loop documentation is becoming a funding and contract requirement. Previously missed; first reported here.
